# 🌿 Introduction

Every child deserves access to nutritious food and a healthy start in life.
Yet millions of children around the world still struggle to get the nutrition they need.

This report explores:

* 🥗 Access to protein-rich foods for children
* 🌍 How nutrition varies across countries
* 📉 Whether things are improving over time

Using UNICEF data, we identify where children are most at risk and what factors influence these outcomes.

---

# Understanding the Data

```{python}
#| label: load-data

import polars as pl
from plotnine import *
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

ind1 = pl.read_csv("unicef_indicator_1.csv", schema_overrides={"time_period": pl.Utf8})
meta = pl.read_csv("unicef_metadata.csv", schema_overrides={"year": pl.Utf8})

ind1 = ind1.rename({col: col.strip() for col in ind1.columns})
meta = meta.rename({col: col.strip() for col in meta.columns})

ind1_total = ind1.filter(pl.col("sex") == "Total")

ind1_total = ind1_total.rename({
    "obs_value": "food_consumption_pct",
    "time_period": "time_period_str",
    "country": "country_name"
})

ind1_total = ind1_total.with_columns(
    pl.col("time_period_str").str.extract(r"(\d{4})").cast(pl.Float64).alias("year")
)

meta_clean = meta.select([
    "country", "alpha_3_code", "year",
    "GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$)",
    "Life expectancy at birth, total (years)"
]).rename({
    "country": "country_name_meta",
    "GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$)": "gdp_per_capita",
    "Life expectancy at birth, total (years)": "life_expectancy"
})

meta_clean = meta_clean.with_columns(
    pl.col("year").cast(pl.Float64)
)

meta_clean = meta_clean.drop_nulls(subset=["gdp_per_capita", "life_expectancy"])

merged = ind1_total.join(meta_clean, on=["alpha_3_code", "year"], how="inner")

plot_data = merged.drop_nulls(subset=["food_consumption_pct", "gdp_per_capita"])
```


* Total observations: **276 country-year records**
* Food consumption ranges from **11% to 94%**
* Most data comes from **lower-income countries**
* Median year: **2016 (recent data)**

---

# 1. Global Distribution of Child Nutrition (World Map)

This map describes a global overview of how child nutrition varies across countries.

```{python}
#| label: world-map
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-align: center

import json
import urllib.request
import pandas as pd

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johan/world.geo.json/master/countries.geo.json"

with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response:
    geo = json.load(response)

rows = []
group_id = 0

for feature in geo["features"]:
    code = feature["id"]
    geom = feature["geometry"]

    if geom is None:
        continue

    if geom["type"] == "Polygon":
        for poly in geom["coordinates"]:
            group_id += 1
            for coord in poly:
                rows.append({
                    "alpha_3_code": code,
                    "group_id": group_id,
                    "long": coord[0],
                    "lat": coord[1]
                })

    elif geom["type"] == "MultiPolygon":
        for multi in geom["coordinates"]:
            for poly in multi:
                group_id += 1
                for coord in poly:
                    rows.append({
                        "alpha_3_code": code,
                        "group_id": group_id,
                        "long": coord[0],
                        "lat": coord[1]
                    })

map_df = pl.DataFrame(rows)

latest = plot_data.sort("year", descending=True).group_by("alpha_3_code").first()

map_data = map_df.join(latest, on="alpha_3_code", how="left")

map_pd = map_data.to_pandas()

(
    ggplot(map_pd, aes(x='long', y='lat', group='group_id', fill='food_consumption_pct')) +
    geom_polygon(color='white', size=0.1) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors=['#EF476F', '#FFD166', '#06D6A0', '#118AB2']) +
    theme_void()
)
```

📌 Children in some regions—especially parts of Africa and South Asia—have significantly lower access to nutritious food.

# 2. GDP vs Nutrition (Scatter Plot)

This chart shows how a country’s wealth relates to child nutrition.

```{python}
#| label: scatter
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

scatter_pd = plot_data.to_pandas()

(
    ggplot(scatter_pd, aes(x='gdp_per_capita', y='food_consumption_pct')) +
    geom_point(aes(color='food_consumption_pct'), alpha=0.6) +
    geom_smooth(method='lm', color='#C73E1D', alpha=0.15) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_color_gradientn(colors=['#EF476F','#FFD166','#06D6A0','#118AB2']) +
    theme_minimal()
)
```

📌 Economic growth improves nutrition—but not consistently across all countries.

---

# 3. Has Nutrition Improved Over Time? (Trend)

This chart shows how global nutrition has changed over the years.

```{python}
#| label: trend
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

ts_data = plot_data.group_by("year").agg(
    pl.col("food_consumption_pct").mean().alias("avg_consumption")
)

ts_pd = ts_data.to_pandas()

(
    ggplot(ts_pd, aes(x='year', y='avg_consumption')) +
    geom_line(color='#2E86AB') +
    geom_point(color='#A23B72') +
    geom_smooth(method='lm', color='#F18F01', alpha=0.15) +
    theme_minimal()
)
```

📌 There is gradual improvement, but progress remains uneven.

---

# 4. Nutrition by Income Group

This chart compares nutrition levels across income groups.

```{python}
#| label: income
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

latest = plot_data.sort("year", descending=True).group_by("alpha_3_code").first()

latest = latest.with_columns(
    pl.when(pl.col("gdp_per_capita") < 1000).then(pl.lit("Low"))
    .when(pl.col("gdp_per_capita") < 4000).then(pl.lit("Lower-Middle"))
    .when(pl.col("gdp_per_capita") < 12000).then(pl.lit("Upper-Middle"))
    .otherwise(pl.lit("High"))
    .alias("income_group")
)

grouped = latest.group_by("income_group").agg(
    pl.col("food_consumption_pct").mean().alias("food_consumption_pct")
)

grouped = grouped.with_columns(
    pl.col("food_consumption_pct").round(1).cast(pl.Utf8).alias("label")
)

grouped_pd = grouped.to_pandas()

(
    ggplot(grouped_pd, aes(x='income_group', y='food_consumption_pct', fill='food_consumption_pct')) +
    geom_col(width=0.7) +
    
    # ✅ SINGLE COLOR GRADIENT (PURPLE SHADES)
    scale_fill_gradient(
        low="#c8e6c9",   # light shade
        high="#1b5e20"   # dark shade
    ) +
    
    geom_text(
        aes(label='label'),
        va='bottom',
        size=9
    ) +
    
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend_position="none")   # remove legend for cleaner look
)
```

📌 Lower-income countries clearly face greater challenges.

# 🔍 Key Findings

* Wide inequality exists
* Economic factors influence outcomes
* Progress is uneven
* Disparities remain

---

# Conclusion

This report shows that:

* Many countries still have low access to nutritious food
* Wealth helps—but is not the only factor
* Progress is happening, but slowly
* Inequality remains a major issue

Every child deserves equal access to nutrition and a healthy future 🌍
